messages:
anya: Quick question from docs review: should we standardize on a single header for 'route status' or separate headers for reason + state? trying to keep SDK surface tiny.

sam: single header is simpler for most clients. e.g. Redwood-Route-Status: normal|degraded|fallback|unavailable. then a separate opt-in header for reason if you need it.

jorge: +1 single header. but we should reserve Redwood-Fallback-Tag for programmatic reasons (quota, capacity, model-variance). it can be absent for normal.

tia: important note: some customers parse status from body only. we should have a canonical small body fallback for older clients: {"rw_status":"degraded","rw_tag":"quota"} when content-type is application/json.

anya: good call. for HTTP codes: proposal from product: keep 200 for valid responses including degraded/fallback; 429 for quota; 503 for infra outages; 502 for upstream model crashes. thoughts?

sam: agree. 200+status header for quality fallbacks avoids app-level retries. 429 must include Retry-After and quota_remaining in body.

jorge: also consider 409 for tenant budget conflicts? we already use 409 elsewhere. maybe reuse 429 + tag=budget to avoid proliferation.

tia: telemetry side: emit metric route_status_count{state,tag,route,region} and histogram of latency per state. console can show state breakdown and allow filtering by model_variant and tenant.

anya: console UX: show a badge per route: green/yellow/red based on 24h percent degraded. thresholds: yellow if degraded>2% and >100 requests, red if >5% and >1k requests. open to suggestions.

sam: those thresholds seem reasonable. add automatic canary rollback if newly deployed variant causes red within 30m of rollout.

jorge: we must be careful with auto-rollbacks; ops teams want to triage. suggest auto-create a canary issue and mute auto-scaling policies for the rollout while alerting on call.

tia: logs problem: headers not always captured in centralized logs. propose adding a tiny trace/span attribute client_visible_status that mirrors the header so we can query traces even when headers drop.

anya: good. for SDKs: expose a Response.metadata object with is_degraded bool, fallback_tag (optional), human_message (optional). do NOT auto-retry. provide helper function showFallbackBanner().

sam: also add a helper to surface a reason link to console: include console_url in 429/503 bodies and in hint object for 200-degraded when Accept: application/redwood+json.

jorge: small example bodies for docs: 
429 body: {"error":"quota_exceeded","retry_after":60,"quota_remaining":0,"console_url":"https://console/redwood/tenants/123/usage"} 
200 degraded hint: {"rw_status":"degraded","rw_tag":"capacity","hint":"served by smaller model, consider dedicated"}

tia: action items:
- telemetry: add route_status_count + client_visible_status tag (jorge)
- SDK: implement Response.metadata + banner helper (anya)
- console: add route badge + auto-create canary task (sam)
- docs: publish mapping table and example bodies (anya)

deploy-bot: deploy:config v3 -> route-status-headers + telemetry flag enabled in canary (12% traffic) :rocket:

anya: canary note: please run a synthetic job that generates degraded responses so we can validate alert noise.

sam: will do. one more: make sure we version the header names in the RFC (v1) so we can change names later without breaking older SDKs.

jorge: ack. i'll add draft RFC with examples and telemetry queries.

tia: thanks all. keeping this lightweight should make adoption easy.

anya: thanks! I'll push the docs PR and tag reviewers.
